name: page-boundaries
about: Where a page number turns. The book has no intrinsic page, so the number is derived: a word offset and a quantum in, a 1-based page out. That derivation exists twice — once on the server, as the definitional reference, and once in the reader, which is what a person actually sees. Two hand-written mirrors drift. These cases are the contract between them: both suites assert every one, so a change on either side that breaks agreement fails a test rather than quietly shipping two different books.

cases.why: The book's first word opens page 1, not page 0.
One word in is still the first page.
The last word of the first page.
The exact quantum boundary turns the page.
Just past the boundary, still the page it opened.
The last word of the second page.
The second boundary; the count never resets.
Deep into the book — numbering is book-global, so a later chapter continues rather than restarting.
A chapter that starts mid-page: its first word is not a page's first word.
The quantum is the server's, not a constant; a different one moves every boundary.
A negative offset cannot exist in a book; it clamps to the first page rather than producing page 0.
A misconfigured quantum reads as page 1 rather than dividing by zero on a read path.
A negative quantum degrades the same way — the guard is on non-positive, not on zero alone.
Both guards at once still yield the first page, never a negative or a zero.
